newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares slump 2.73 pct in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares slump 2.73 pct in thin trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended early losses in afternoon selling on Monday amid liquidity shortage as political uneasiness, first quarter profits and April inflation figures irritated the market, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,392, down 39 points, or 2.73 percent from Friday after rebounding slightly from a late low of 1,388. Daily volume dropped to 9.81 trillion lira ($72 million) from Friday's 10.67 trillion ($78.8 million).

"I expect the general direction to be downward until prices bottom out or there is a positive political development. Reaction buys at the current levels will be short-lived," said Cem Baycan from Delta securities.
Brokers who await major support at the index's 1,380 level after the shattering of 1,420 and 1,400 supports today, said fresh liquidity influx was necessary for a lasting recovery.
They said sentiment soured as many companies released poor first quarter results on Monday and April consumer inflation, released on Sunday, came out above market expectations.

The market index had dived 6.6 percent in the past seven days amid political worries over the fate of the Islamist-led coalition government after the market opened on April 24 following a 6-1/2 day holiday.
